title: Native whole-system reduction counit computes on K-flat complexes
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell and a scheme W. Let S be any recorded CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus for E on W. Let P be an arbitrary unbounded K-flat complex of modules over the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For the ordinary quotient/limit adjunction and the derived-limit-normalized mate systemReductionCounit of [def-pur-native-reduction-counit-data], its component at the homotopy class of P is an isomorphism from S.reduction(Qh(P)) to Qh(ordinaryReduction(P)). This assertion is on the native whole sequence site, before constant-scalar restriction, scalar extension to a second field, or arithmetic restriction. It has no completeness or constructibility hypothesis and includes the zero complex and empty site.

source.place: Lemma derived-base-change (06YY), section-derived-limits (0940), lemma-derived-limit-is-ok (0941); literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors. The quotient extension is the sequence-site specialization; its inverse-image part is exact constant diagram formation.

proof.text: View the ordinary quotient-system functor as constant diagram formation followed by extension to the actual quotient-ring sheaf on the sequence site. The ordinary right adjoint is inverse limit after coefficient restriction, so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies this ordinary functor with ordinaryReduction. This identification uses its ordinary adjunction unit.

Constant diagram formation is exact, and its tensor with any acyclic sequence complex is acyclic at each level when P is K-flat. Thus its value on P is K-flat. Extension to the quotient sequence ring computes derived extension on this K-flat complex, by the same tensor-restriction adjunction argument used for ordinary change of rings. Consequently the canonical computing counit from derived ordinary quotient extension to ordinaryReduction is invertible at P.

The derived quotient-extension/limit adjunction identifies its right adjoint with the right derived functor of ordinaryLimit. The recorded reductionRightComparison identifies that functor with coefficientSequenceLimit and fixes the unit on every whole-system complex. Unique left-adjoint comparison therefore identifies the derived quotient extension with S.reduction. Under adjoint transposition its computing counit is exactly the mate of the right-derived unit, namely systemReductionCounit. This proves invertibility of its component at P. The argument applies to arbitrary unbounded K-flat P; flat terms are not required for the pure change-of-rings tensor computation, since the constant diagram functor is exact.

proof_origin.place: The native quotient-extension computation in the proof of lem-pur-scalar-target-counit-universal, before scalar extension and exact restrictions. Adjoint uniqueness and unit normalization identify the precise mate.

theorem nativeReductionCounit_kFlat (W : Scheme.{u})
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus.{u, u} l E W)
    (P : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients
      (R := completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E W) P) :
    IsIso ((systemReductionCounit l E W S).app
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj P))
